Inglewood, California
  October 10, 2023

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
October 10, 2023, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:01 p.m.

The Acting City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present: Mayor Butts, Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk;
  and
  Absent: None.

City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Angela Allen  Acting City Clerk
  Ken Campos  City Attorney
  Christine Padilla  Staff Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEMS. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on the
Closed Session Item Nos. CS-1, CS-2, and CS-3.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:01 p.m. for Closed Session Item
Nos. CS-1, CS-2, and CS-3.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the hour
of 2:01 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Gray, Padilla,
  Morales, Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any item
on the Agendas.

There was no response.
 October 10, 2023

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated October
  6, 2023, in the amount of $6,884,293.61, are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor
  Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said
  registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/ Successor Agency Members/ Housing Authority Members Gray,
  Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/ Successor Agency Chairman/ Housing
  Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Faulk that the Minutes for the City Council Meeting held on August 22, 2023, be approved.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

125  CLAIMS DENIED. Letter from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claims pursuant to Government Code, Section 913:
  1. Gloria Gonzalez-Karch for alleged personal injury; unmarked cement and/or brick wall
  (near SoFi Stadium; 1001 Stadium Dr.) on March 10, 2023.
  2. Wenceslao Lemus for alleged personal injury; sidewalk slip and fall on August 15, 2023.
  3. Cindy Mendez and Elsa Mendez for alleged property damage; unkept City tree on May
  14, 2023.
  4. Mark Sanders for alleged property damage; City negligence/liability not described on
  September 5, 2023.
  5. Jeffrey Stevenson for alleged personal injury; Vincent Park Homeless Encampment
  Cleanup on August 15, 2023.
  6. Jennifer Villarruel for alleged personal injury; uneven and/or broken pavement (at/or
  near SoFi Stadium; 1001 Stadium Dr.) on March 10, 2023.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby Reject Claims listed as A-1 through A-6. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

173  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – SHAFFER PSYCHOLOGICAL INSTITUTE. Staff
  report dated October 10, 2023, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council
  Members authorize the payment of an outstanding invoice submitted by Shaffer
  Psychological Institute, for Fitness-for-Duty Evaluation services.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of $2,800. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 24-010 APPROVED – 40 LOVE
  FOUNDATION, INC.; RESOLUTION NO. 24-04 ADOPTED - AMENDING THE
  FISCAL YEAR 2023-24 BUDGET. Staff report dated October 10, 2023, was presented
  recommending that the Mayor and Council Members award a contract and approve a five
  (5)-year agreement with 40 Love Foundation, Inc., for the provision of Tennis Management
  Services, per RFP-0209.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Award contract and approve Agreement No. 24-010 in the
  amount of $503,190 for Year One (total amount of $3,057,490); and 2) Adopt Resolution
  No. 24-04 entitled:

  2
 October 10, 2023

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-24 BUDGET TO
  COVER EXPENDITURES FOR TENNIS MANAGEMENT SERVICES

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – AUNDRAE RUSSELL. Staff report dated October 10,
  2023, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members authorize the
  payment of an invoice submitted by Aundrae Russell, for Master of Ceremonies services
  rendered at the National Night Out event.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of $1,000. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171  STAFF TO PURSUE STATE LICENSING AUTHORIZED – CITY’S EARLY
  LEARNERS PLAY TO LEARN CHILDHOOD DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM. Staff
  report dated October 10, 2023, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council
  Members authorize staff to pursue State licensing of the City’s Early Learners Play to Learn
  Childhood Development Program.
  Sabrina Barnes, Park, Recreation and Community Services Director, presented a brief oral
  report.
  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Gray that
  the City Council does hereby authorize staff to pursue State licensing. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

127  COUNCIL MEMBER MORALES COMMENTS. Council Member Morales stated
  that he remembered starting over 20 years ago working for the Council, and Sabrina  Barnes
  took him around and showed him the parks when he was young. He also stated that  he
  remembered those days and the people who were nice to him. He mentioned  losing the old
  pieces of Inglewood that mattered, and those are the ones that are felt. He also mentioned the
  new pieces that were also good. Finally, he discussed Sabrina helping  him with his dad
  before becoming a Council Member, and he thanked her for that.

127  COUNCIL MEMBER GRAY COMMENTS. Council Member Gray asked Sabrina to
  stick around because she wanted to mention her retirement in her final remarks.

127  COUNCIL MEMBER PADILLA COMMENTS. Council Member Padilla mentioned
  a previous conversation with Sabrina, where he thanked her for being herself, always being
  true to who she was, and always helping others. He stated that Sabrina has always been
  inspirational, loving, caring, and, more than anything, giving. Council Member Padilla also
  noted that Sabrina had a servant’s heart for 30-plus years, and Inglewood has benefited
  tremendously. Additionally, he stated that he would miss her being there every day, but she
  will forever have a place in the City of Inglewood. Furthermore, he added that she was part of
  the family, and it was an honor and pleasure to have worked with her as they moved  the city
  forward. Finally, he congratulated Sabrina on her retirement and wished her the best.

  3
 October 10, 2023

127  COUNCIL MEMBER FAULK COMMENTS. Council Member Faulk stated that
  she found it interesting that this program meant so much to Sabrina Barnes that she  made
  this her final staff report before she retired. She expressed that as a mother of two,  she
  knew how vital this program would be to working families, especially single parents  who
  struggle with child care. She mentioned that a program of this caliber would change  the
  game and quoted the Mayor talking about changing the game. Council Member Faulk
  thanked Sabrina for making this the last important program that she would implement in
  the City of Inglewood because it would be one of the most critical programs that the city
  could do. Additionally, she thanked Sabrina for being the best Director the city or any  other
  city has ever seen. Finally, Council Member Faulk concluded there will never be another
  Sabrina Barnes.

173  ORDINANCE NO. 24-01 ADOPTED – ESTABLISH SALARIES AND
  CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024. Staff report
  dated October 10, 2023, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members
  adopt Ordinance No. 24-01, establishing pay range assignment and conditions of
  employment for Fiscal Year 2023-2024.
  It was moved by Council Member Padilla, and seconded by Council Member Morales that
  further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, it was moved by Council Member Padilla, and seconded by Council Member
  Faulk that Ordinance No. 24-01 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA,
  ESTABLISHING PAY RANGE ASSIGNMENT AND CONDITIONS OF
  EMPLOYMENT FOR THE VARIOUS OFFICERS, EMPLOYEES AND
  POSITIONS IN THE SERVICE OF THE CITY FOR FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024;
  INCLUDING THE INGLEWOOD TRANSIT CONNECTOR (ITC) GRANT
  FUNDED TRANSITIONAL APPOINTMENTS AND REPEALING ALL
  PREVIOUS ORDINANCES OF THE CITY IN CONFLICT OR AT VARIANCE
  HEREWITH; THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, DOES ORDAIN AS FOLLOWS:

  which was introduced at the meeting held on October 10, 2023, be adopted. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

132.6  CLOSED SESSION – PENDING LITIGATION – MANUEL DUSKIN V. CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, ET AL.; LASC CASE NO. 21STCV33683. Closed Session –
  Confidential – Attorney/Client Privileged; City Council Conference with Legal Counsel
  regarding pending litigation pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1); Manuel
  Duskin v. City of Inglewood, et al.; LASC Case No.: 21STCV33683.

  Discussion held; Status provided.

132.6  CLOSED SESSION – PENDING LITIGATION – ROSANNE GERMEILLE V. CITY
  OF INGLEWOOD; LASC CASE NO. 19STCV05275. Closed Session – Confidential –
  Attorney/Client Privileged; City Council Conference with Legal Counsel regarding pending
  litigation pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1); Rosanne Germeille v. City
  of Inglewood; LASC Case No.: 19STCV05275.

  Discussion held; Direction given to staff.

132.6  CLOSED SESSION – PENDING LITIGATION – DAVID WILLIAMS V. CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD; LASC CASE NO. 21STCV44435. Closed Session – Confidential –
  Attorney/Client Privileged; City Council Conference with Legal Counsel regarding pending
  litigation pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1); David Williams v. City of
  Inglewood; LASC Case No.: 21STCV44435.

  4
 October 10, 2023

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve the request for settlement. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  REPORTS – CITY MANAGER. City Manager Artie Fields thanked Sabrina Barnes for
  all her years of service and the years of service for the past 11-plus years that he has been
  City Manager. He stated that Sabrina has been a standout department head and will be
  missed. The City Manager mentioned that when he was the Assistant City Manager
  for West Covina, he had the opportunity to be the Interim Human Resources
  Director or the Interim Parks and Recreation Director. He discussed how Parks and
  Recreation Directors have to work harder because every weekend, something is going on
  in the City. Additionally, he discussed the directors giving up much of their lives every
  weekend to attend every event and Sabrina dedicating much of her life to the City.
  Finally, he expressed his appreciation and stated the community is better.

  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. City Clerk Aisha L. Thompson wished Sabrina Barnes a
  farewell and said she would be missed. She thanked her for the services that she provided
  to young people and seniors. She stated that she allowed so many opportunities for the
  community to thrive. The City Clerk reiterated what Council Member Morales stated
  about Sabrina opening her arms when she was Deputy City Clerk. She added that when she
  took office as City Clerk, her arms were extended more expansively, and she was thankful.
  Finally, she thanked Sabrina again and wished her well.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished
  to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not elsewhere
  considered on the Agenda.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) spoke concerning the City providing Spanish translation when
  Spanish speakers talk to allow the public to understand what they are saying. He also
  spoke about evening meetings. He stated that the City Council should have evening
  meetings so that residents who work and take care of their families could attend the
  meetings. Finally, he stated that he would appreciate it if his request for evening meetings
  was honored.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) spoke emotionally about Sabrina Barnes' retirement. He stated
  that Sabrina was more significant than the Parks and Recreation Department. He stated that
  he gave her trouble at the library.

  Charlotte Williams spoke concerning the Mayor and Council Members signing a
  resolution to remove Cuba from the State's Sponsored List of Terrorists. She stated that
  recently, many sister cities around the country have signed, including the Los Angeles
  County Federation of Labor and the American Postal Workers Union AFL CIO of San
  Francisco. She also stated that she had been to Cuba twice, and it was a very beautiful
  country. She discussed Trump's presidency, who put Cuba on the sponsored list of
  terrorists, and her belief in why. Additionally, she discussed Cuba sending doctors to the
  United States during COVID-19 and the vote taken each year to remove Cuba from the
  state's list. She petitioned the Council to end the 60-year-old blockade because Los
  Angeles had yet to sign the resolution after a visit to their Council Meeting. Furthermore,
  she added that she was an Inglewood resident and hoped Inglewood would beat Los
  Angeles in signing. Finally, she reiterated the cities that signed the resolution and hoped
  the Council would sign it.
